lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Over a hundred students say a silver disc dropped behind their school.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Melburn, April nineteen sixty-six. At morning break, students and a teacher look up at a round, silent, silver shape.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: A science teacher says it rose again, a silver streak chased by five light planes.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: But a check later shows no commercial, private, or air force pilot reported anything unusual.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The next day's paper says: perhaps a weather balloon, released miles away.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Students find flattened grass, but accounts vary between one circle and three.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Air force men search the field and find nothing. The landowner burns the grass.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Skeptics say one plane may have towed a target drohg. No record of such an exercise was found.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: So was it a balloon and a drohg, or a silver disc behind their school?
